notes:
User is meal-prepping healthy lunches and recently bought a new Instant Pot and Air Fryer. They enjoy practical, protein- and fiber-rich bean/lentil meals, recently made chili con carne, and considered bean/lentil chili. They are planning a Cuban Black Bean and Rice Bowl with air-fried sweet potato fries and a simple fresh fruit salad. Fruit salad ingredients suggested: strawberries, grapes, kiwi, pineapple, lime, optional mint and sugar.

Air Fryer fries guidance: cut sweet potatoes evenly into thin sticks, soak in cold water for at least 30 minutes, dry thoroughly, lightly oil, and avoid overcrowding. Air Fryer at 400°F/200°C for roughly 12–15 minutes, shaking halfway; adjust for fryer and desired crispiness. Season near the end to avoid burning spices. For leftovers, cool promptly and refrigerate in a vented container lined with paper towel for up to about 2–3 days; briefly re-crisp in Air Fryer. Do not leave cooked fries at room temperature or store them in a pantry. For longer storage, freeze fully cooked fries in a single layer, then bag/container once frozen; reheat from frozen in Air Fryer around 400°F for 5–7 minutes or oven until hot/crispy.

Cuban Black Bean and Rice Bowl: sauté black beans with onion, bell pepper, and garlic; serve over brown rice with avocado and lime. Leftovers may be refrigerated in shallow airtight containers for 3–4 days or frozen for 2–3 months. Refrigerate within 2 hours; do not leave large portions to cool at room temperature. Reheat only the portion needed to 165°F/74°C.

They previously prepared or planned Korean Chicken Stew (Jjimdak) using boneless chicken breast, reducing gochugaru from 2 to 1 tbsp because they are sensitive to heat. They appreciate spice adjustments, practical substitutions, and may return with cooking feedback. Chicken should reach 165°F; breast can dry out, so adding thighs could improve texture.
trajectory:
User is meal-prepping healthy lunches and recently bought a new Instant Pot. They are interested in make-ahead soups/stews that can be reheated, especially Korean-inspired dishes. They are preparing Korean Chicken Stew (Jjimdak) and chose boneless chicken breast rather than thighs/drumsticks. They are unfamiliar with gochujang and were concerned about heat, so they plan to reduce gochugaru/Korean chili flakes from 2 to 1 tablespoon and adjust after tasting.

Recipe discussed: 1 lb bite-size chicken breast, 2 potatoes, 2 carrots, 1 large onion, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp gochujang, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp gochugaru (their chosen amount), 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp black pepper, 2 cups chicken broth, sesame oil, and optional green onions. Cooker steps discussed: sauté chicken and remove; sauté aromatics/vegetables; combine seasonings, broth, and chicken; pressure cook for about 10–12 minutes at high pressure, followed by a natural release; then season and garnish. Check chicken reaches 165°F/74°C. Chicken breast may dry out; using a mix of breast and thighs is an option.

User appreciates guidance on spiciness and practical substitutions. They were about to begin preparing ingredients and may return with cooking questions or feedback.
